Investor guide

What is cap rate, and what it doesn't tell you

Cap rate is the quickest way to compare income properties. It's also easy to misread.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
2-minute readFor investorsFormula + example

01The formula

Cap rate = net operating income ÷ price

Gross rent
$31,800
− Vacancy (3%)
−$954
− Operating expenses
−$11,700
= Net operating income
$19,146
÷ Price
$600,000
Cap rate
3.19%

Same example as the cash flow guide. Net operating income excludes mortgage payments.

02What cap rate leaves out

Financing

Not included

Two buyers of the same property get the same cap rate, whatever their mortgage.

Price changes

Not included

Appreciation or a falling market isn't in the number.

Condition

Not included

A roof due next year doesn't show up in this year's NOI.

Rent upside

Not included

Below-market rents, or units first occupied after Nov 15, 2018 that aren't under the rent guideline.

03Cap rate vs. cash-on-cash return

Cap rate

NOI ÷ price

Works best when

  • Comparing properties to each other
  • Quick screening of listings

Watch out for

  • Ignores your mortgage and down payment

Cash-on-cash

Annual cash flow ÷ cash you invested

Works best when

  • Comparing to other uses of your money
  • Seeing the effect of your financing

Watch out for

  • Changes with every rate and down payment
Ali's take

Use cap rate to compare listings, then cash flow to decide. A property can have a decent cap rate and still cost you every month.
